decisions.final:
The purpose of a likelihood scale is to make judgements from different assessors, business lines and periods comparable. Verbal labels alone do not achieve that, because studies of probability language consistently show that the same word maps to widely different probabilities for different people. Anchoring each level to a frequency band removes the ambiguity:

| Level | Qualitative rating | Frequency of occurrence | Probability of occurrence (one-year horizon) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Remote | Less than once in 20 years | < 5% |
| 2 | Unlikely | Once in 5 to 20 years | 5% to 20% |
| 3 | Possible | Once in more than 1 up to 5 years | 20% to 50% |
| 4 | Likely | Once a year or more often | > 50% |

This is the four-point likelihood scale shown in the reading (Chapelle, Ch. 4); firms may calibrate their own bands, but each level must carry an explicit frequency or probability anchor.

Two further design points. The number of levels should be small enough that assessors can discriminate reliably between adjacent levels; a fifteen-point scale offers precision the underlying judgement cannot support and simply relocates the disagreement. And likelihood and impact are different dimensions measured in different units, so they are plotted against one another rather than summed. That is what a heatmap is for.
decisions.reason: Source Q30 (p.27) matches the JSON exactly, so this is a source issue, not an extraction error. Key (a) is correct. However the worked table (Rare <1 in 10y; Unlikely 3-10y; Possible 1-3y; Likely >=1/yr) is the only concrete scale the candidate sees and conflicts with the curriculum's four-point scale (notes/FRM_Consolidated_Vol1/ch/32_OR_ORR4.tex lines 122-141: Likely >=1/yr >50%; Possible >1-5y 20-50%; Unlikely 1 in 5-20y 5-20%; Remote <1 in 20y <5%). Auditor's diagnosis is right, but its proposed value was only a table fragment with an 'Alternatively...' note embedded, not an applicable value; final gives the full solution text with the curriculum table and a one-line note that it is the reading's scale. Options, key, optionAnalysis and trap unaffected (option (a)'s 'once in ten years or less often' is only an illustrative example of a frequency band and remains fine).
